utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-94-2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Dragan Nikolic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To start with, my apologies for starting a quarter of an hour late. This was due to my ignorance of the streets in The Hague. I just got completely lost. Anyway -- which is not the first time that it has happened to me, but it is the first time it has happened on my way to the Tribunal from where I was. So my apologies once more. The second thing is I welcome you to this Status Conference again, and I would like to address myself to the accused. Mr. Nikolic, can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honour. I'm Upawansa Yapa, appearing for the Prosecution, with Ms. Patricia Sellers and Mr. William Smith. Ms. Diane Boles is our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you. Appearances for the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Howard Morrison for the accused Dragan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you. As you will certainly recall the last Status Conference, which I presided myself, was held on the 18th of March. And this Status Conference, which hopefully will be the last one before the trial commences, is being held in terms of Rule 65 bis, although a few days after the 120 days established. But that, I understand, you are -- you know the reason for that. And it's just necessary to repeat or to remind you that the purpose of the Status Conference, amongst other things, is to ensure the proper and expeditious preparation for the trial and to give an opportunity to the accused, personally or through his counsel, to raise issues in relation to his mental or physical condition. And this is precisely the first thing that I want to address. Mr. Nikolic, do you have any complaints related to your detention here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Now, I think we can, on the basis of that, proceed fairly quickly. And before we do, I think I owe it to you, both Prosecution and Defence, following the information that has been given to me by the senior legal officer for Trial Chamber II, Mr. Von Hebel, and that is to show publicly my appreciation for your cooperation and flexibility shown in the course of the meeting which -- of which he presided recently, in terms of Rule 65 ter. I mean, he did report to me the outcome of that meeting, and he did also report to me how positive your contribution was and how appreciated your cooperation is. And it is, I think, my duty to reiterate that and say it in -- publicly in an open session. The first significant matter is -- or most -- perhaps the most important matter on our agenda today is the decision, pending decision, on the motion on a legal arrest. I know that you have already been sufficiently informed during this -- the meeting that I have referred to, but I can also confirm on my part here that the decision itself has been elaborated in the first and the second and the third draft. There are a few items that are being discussed -- still being discussed between the other two Judges forming -- constituting this Trial Chamber - that's Judge Schomburg and Judge Mumba - I can assure you that there are no problems ahead and we should be in -- certainly without hesitation and I can confirm that we should be in a position to hand down our decision within a fairly short time. We could actually hand it down within an even shorter time, but I'm sure you would understand that we have August arriving and that creates some problems. So the idea is to hand down the decision before the end of August, when hopefully - and not only the three Judges, but also the more important members of the staff dealing with this case - will be present here in The Hague. So do expect a definitive decision before the end of August, and that, whichever way it goes, that will be a decision which I suppose will go to appeal. It's that kind of decision in any case, and I mean, you understand that -- I'm sure you understand that. That would be the latest. If we are in a position to hand down the judgement before, we will hand down the judgement before. I want you to understand that the three of us will be in close contact regularly during the month of August, also because this is not the only case that we are dealing with collectively. We are working on it -- it's practically finished as far as I am concerned. I mean, a few cosmetic interventions that we need to take. That would be about it. And we should be in a position to issue -- hand down the judgement. Then I know that -- before I pass on to something different, do you have any comments on -- any remarks on this issue? Mr. Morrison, in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. Plainly, it is a matter which is likely to go to appeal. We discussed this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'd imagine that. Yes. Whichever way it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Whichever way it goes. Because the issues are -- some of the issues are fairly fundamental.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: The only concern we have jointly as to that is the impact of that upon any trial date. We discussed that matter yesterday with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: -- the senior legal officer. I think the general view was that to proceed, as it were, planning for trial and take the appeal, if any, as and when it comes and deal with it as expeditiously as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And as far as that goes, Mr. Morrison, I can assure you that we're talking of a time frame where that would be perfectly possible, also because we have been working in recent days on the programme for sittings, a draft calendar for sittings between now and the end of the year, and this is taken care of already. Obviously I cannot anticipate dates -- promise dates, et cetera, but it's something that has been taken care of in anticipation of the fact that there will certainly be an appeal whichever way it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. The next thing -- and on this I am advised that -- it may just be relevant to bring out or to mention at this -- in this Status Conference is the issue with regard to disclosure. I understand that this matter is more or less in hand, that there are very few, possibly two statements under Rule 66 which will soon be disclosed to you, Mr. Morrison, and another five statements that are in the process of being translated. And you know that that is a problem, particularly in the wake of certain cases that have been started here, certain trials that have been started here. However, I have the assurance through my senior legal officer but from the Prosecution that this would be -- it's very well in hand and they should be made available to you, Mr. Morrison, within a fairly short time. I am also informed - and of course, if there is any information to the contrary, please do let me know - that the Prosecution has completed its obligations of disclosure under Rule 68. If you have reason to doubt that or any submissions to make, Mr. Morrison, please do. Tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. I am -- I have been so informed by the Prosecution. I have absolutely no reason to believe to the contrary. In fact, I don't believe to the contrary. I accept that this is a prosecution being conducted absolutely bona fide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And then there is the important aspect of agreed facts. I told Mr. Von Hebel this morning that I wish the Brdjanin/Talic case could proceed on this matter with such flexibility. I understand that you are in the process of preparing a list of agreed facts or facts on which there could be mutual agreement. And if that is so, I do want to again express publicly my appreciation. Yes, Mr. Morrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, yes, that is the case. The Prosecution has delivered a list of 184 different matters, upon which they've asked for agreement. Those matters which are plainly contentious as between the Defence and the Prosecution, obviously we cannot agree. Those are matters which are issued in trial. There are a considerable number of peripheral issues which we can agree and we have agreed. And what I have done today is I've handed over the responses to the Prosecutor. Some of it will require the re-drafting of admissions by the Prosecution. And that having been done, I anticipate there will then be complete agreement the object of the exercise being that when the case comes to trial, we will have but a single document to put before the Court rather than a Prosecution document with a Defence document in opposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's -- yes. I thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Your Honour, two matters that I wish to take up at this moment, Your Honour. In regard to the Rule 68 disclosure, I wanted to mention this matter. Your Honour stated that we have informed the senior legal officer that it is complete. We do not wish to use the word "complete" in respect of Rule 68 disclosure. So far as maybe up to date, whatever that had to be disclosed we have, and the searches are going on. And if you do come across any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: So it is an ongoing process and we'll be doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: In respect of the agreed facts, as my learned friend correctly stated, we have tendered the document to him with matters for agreement, 184, and he has been of great assistance to us and he has indicated to us on which matters he could agree. And finally what we propose to do is to submit to Your Honours the document which both of us can agree in respect of the agreed facts, which will assist Your Honours' chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Yapa. And that brings me to the most crucial of -- and most important points in -- on the agenda of this Status Conference, and that is the future. I will try to cut the corner straight away and come to the basics. It is the opinion and a suggestion of this Chamber that the trial itself could start based on the information that was collected by the senior legal officer during the meeting that I mentioned, that the trial could start on the 18th of November of this year. This would entail the following, that the -- namely, one, that the Prosecution would need to file its pre-trial brief by not later than the 3rd of October, followed by the pre-trial brief from the Defence, expected not beyond the 24th of October. Following that there will be a Pre-Trial Conference on approximately the 14th of November, a few days before the commencement of the trial. This is based on the assumption or the information that I have been given that the Prosecution estimates about six to seven weeks for the presentation of its case, that the estimated number of witnesses is roughly between 35 and 40. That does not include the expert witnesses and some Rule 92 bis statements; that the Defence estimates work -- one working month for the presentation of its case, with an estimated number of witnesses of approximately 20, maybe less. And that includes the defendant, if he chooses to give evidence. And it is also based on the anticipation that the Registrar of this Tribunal will appoint a co-counsel by not later than -- or around about the beginning of next month, the beginning of August. I know that this matter is in hand. May I have your comments on this time frame that I am suggesting to you. The Prosecution, would you be in a position to file your pre-trial brief -- this is obviously without prejudice, because you could lose the motion on the illegal arrest. But for the time being, I'm just working on the presumption that it will be on -- in your favour and that the trial will -- will proceed, following also a decision by the Appeals Chamber. So we need to work on that assumption, whichever way it goes. But assuming that that will be the case, would you be in a position to file your pre-trial brief on or about the 3rd of October of this year?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for the inquiry. The dates given by Your Honour are quite acceptable to us, and we -- we are agreeable to those dates. They would not create a problem for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And Mr. Morrison, should that be the case, and assuming that the Prosecution does file its pre-trial on the 3rd of October, 2002 or thereabouts, will you be in a position to file your pre-trial brief on or about the 24th of October of this year?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. That won't be difficult. I'm assured by the Registry that the co-counsel will be appointed about the 1st of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That seems very likely, I'm informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: One of her tasks -- in fact, her principal task is going to be the collation of witnesses that have been seen already by an investigator and the more detailed assessment of their value to the Defence. I anticipate that she will be able to complete that task certainly by the end of September, beginning of October. So I wouldn't have seen any difficulty in complying with the 24th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. So that being the case, there shouldn't be any difficulties for holding a Pre-Trial Conference or about the 14th of November. And in anticipation of another Presiding Judge having terminated the case of which he is presiding -- the trial over which he is presiding now, there shouldn't be difficulties in having the trial -- this trial start on the 18th of November, give and take a couple of days here or there, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Your Honour, looking at my diary, I just noticed one thing. I see that I've been invited to speak at a conference in The Hague on the 14th of November. I'm just wondering whether or not it's possible that the -- the Pre-Trial Conference could take place on the 13th. Or is that not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The 13th would be what day?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wednesday. It shouldn't be -- 13th. That would be even better. Let's mark the 12th or the 13th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: That would be -- that would suit the purposes very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I -- the conference is in The Hague, as it happens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But it so happens that I think I have agreed with the other two Judges in the Brdjanin/Talic case -- Judge Taya needs to go to Japan, and I think we are stopping from the 14th or 15th, something like that. So -- but we -- Mr. Von Hebel will be in -- communicating with you in due course, but we'll take into consideration what you have just stated. And the status -- the Pre-Trial Conference will be held either on the 13th or on the 12th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISON
utterances.text: I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That wouldn't change the trial from starting -- the trial date for the commencement of the trial of -- based on the 18th, hoping that the other trial Judge -- presiding trial Judge will have finished the other case. So that being the case, I think I will proceed with instructing the legal staff to issue an order relating to the timetable in accordance with what I've outlined, subject, of course, to the outcome of the decision on the illegal arrest motion. Is that agreeable? I thank you. And with that, unless there are any other -- there is any other matter that either the Prosecution or the Defence would like to raise at this point, we can adjourn. So the Status Conference is adjourned. I thank you once more for all the cooperation that you have shown throughout. Thank you. And good afternoon to you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
